Reuters reported that Russia's antitrust regulator has officially launched an investigation into Apple, accusing it of failing to pre-install the state-backed instant messaging app MAX and the Russian app store RuStore on its devices. Details are as follows.

Russia files antitrust lawsuit against Apple

Since Russia passed a law in 2019 requiring device manufacturers to provide local apps on products sold in the country, Apple and Russian authorities have been locked in a protracted tug-of-war.

When the law took effect in 2021, Apple reached an arrangement whereby Russian users setting up a new iPhone would be shown a list of recommended Russian-developed apps, rather than having them pre-installed automatically.

In March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Apple promptly halted product sales and exports in the country, and removed the RT News and Sputnik News apps from the App Store outside Russia. That September, Apple also removed several apps owned by Russian tech company VK, citing UK sanctions as the reason.

Last year, Russia began requiring all new smartphones and tablets sold in the country to come pre-installed with the state-backed instant messaging app MAX, while extending the mandate for pre-installation of the RuStore app store to Apple devices. Apple did not comply with either requirement.

Tensions escalated further in June, when Apple first removed MAX from the Russian App Store, and later the same month pulled several apps developed by VK. Apple said the removals were necessary to comply with sanctions.

This prompted Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service (FAS) to order the company to address what it called discriminatory practices against local software by July 15. Apple reportedly partially complied, allowing a Russian search engine to be pre-installed in iOS 26.6, but did not implement the requirements related to MAX and RuStore.

Now, according to Reuters, after Apple failed to fully comply with the warning, Russia has officially launched an antitrust investigation into the company.

It remains unclear what penalties Apple might face if Russia finds it in violation of its competition laws. In 2024, Russia calculated fines against Google totalling approximately 20 decillion dollars (a 2 followed by 33 zeros) for its years-long refusal to reinstate Russian state and pro-Kremlin channels blocked on YouTube.

Apple has not yet responded to the investigation.
